scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge incurred 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Greg Walsh and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Greg, thank you for reaching out. I understand you're looking to recover a charge from a service cancellation that occurred just outside our standard window. I'd be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with the account?
Sure, my account number is 8829301 and the email is g.walsh@email.com.
Thank you, Greg. For security purposes, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and your billing zip code?
The card ends in 4492 and my zip code is 90210.

Thank you for verifying those details. I have located your account and the transaction in question. While our 'Service Terms and Refund Policy' (Section 4.2) states that refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the billing date, I can see your cancellation request was processed successfully on the 34th day. Given your history as a loyal customer, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to this policy.
Oh, that would be wonderful. I appreciate you taking the time to look into it for me.

It is my pleasure, Greg. I have processed the refund of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3-5 business days depending on your financial institution. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the customer's account, acknowledged the policy violation, and utilized an authorized one-time exception to issue a full refund.
